title: Episode One — Two Desks Over
summary: The first school week after joining FC Batavia: a recess World Cup Knockout with a best friend and a rival-club classmate, a group presentation with the same two people, Coach Code's first lesson, the Saturday friendly, and Monday.

lines.text: Monday. The classroom smells like pencil shavings and someone's orange. {teacher} is writing PROJECT on the board in letters that get smaller as she runs out of space.

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: Groups of three, presentations Wednesday. Six minutes, visual cards, everyone speaks. I grade the group, not the loudest person in it.
Two desks over, {rival} is drawing a goal net on the corner of a worksheet. Sonoran United's number ten, and the best player at recess by a distance. {rival} sees you looking.

lines.speaker: rival
lines.text: Heard you signed for Batavia. We've got you in three weeks. Don't worry — I'll be gentle.
A folded note lands on your desk. {friend}'s handwriting: RECESS. WORLD CUP KNOCKOUT. YOU'RE IN. (Not a question.)

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: Eight of us. {rival} plays. Everybody wants to knock {rival} out and nobody ever does. Today's the day. Probably.

response.speaker: friend
response.text: Yes. Okay. Rule one: call for it early. Rule two: don't shoot with the wrong foot in front of {rival}, you'll hear about it for a month.

response.speaker: rival
response.text: Rule three: there are no rules. See you at the bell.

choices.label: "I'll watch today. First day and everything."

response.speaker: friend
response.text: Watch? You don't watch Knockout. Fine. Fine. Tomorrow then.

response.speaker: rival
response.text: Smart. Scout first. That's what I'd do.

lines.text: The far end of the blacktop, one goal chalked on the wall, a strip of grass that counts as the box. Eight players, one server. {friend} bounces the ball once and looks at you like you've already agreed to something.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: Serve comes in, first touch, shoot. Miss, lose it, or dawdle: strike. Three strikes, out. Last one standing wins the World Cup. Which is a tennis ball {ravi} keeps in his bag.

lines.speaker: rival
lines.text: Move before the ball comes. That's the only advice you get from me.
The last serve drops, your touch takes it away from the wall, and the shot is in before anyone has decided whether to cheer. {wck_players} started. One is left. It's you.

lines.speaker: cm-ravi
lines.text: AND THE WORLD CUP GOES TO — hang on, what's your last name —

lines.speaker: rival
lines.text: Fine. Good touch. That doesn't count on Saturdays.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: It counts. It counts so much. I'm telling everyone at training.
Your third strike comes with {wck_place} of {wck_players} still in it — deeper than a first day should get you. {wck_winner} takes the tennis ball.

lines.speaker: rival
lines.text: You made me work for a bit there. I'm not saying that twice.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: Top half on day one. I said you'd be good. Nobody listens.
Strike three arrives fast, the way it does when the ball keeps coming before you've moved. You stand at the wall and watch the rest. {wck_winner} wins it.

lines.speaker: rival
lines.text: You were waiting for the ball. It doesn't wait for you.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: Ignore that. Actually — don't ignore it, it's right, but ignore the face.

lines.speaker: cm-leah
lines.text: First game out first is a tradition. I did it. Ravi did it twice.
The bell goes with the game unfinished, {wck_place} of {wck_players} still in. Nobody won. Everybody claims to have been about to.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: Unfinished. That's a draw. That's basically a win.

lines.speaker: rival
lines.text: That's a Tuesday problem.
You walk off before the game is done. Behind you the serves keep coming; the quiet where your name would have been is louder than the shouting.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: You just — left? In the middle? We had eight. Now we've got seven and a hole.

lines.speaker: rival
lines.text: Huh.
You watch from the fence. Eight in, and it goes the way {friend} said: everyone tries to knock {rival} out and nobody does. {rival} takes the serve moving, first touch already pointing at the wall.

lines.speaker: cm-tobias
lines.text: I'm out first every time. It's fine. Someone has to hold the bags.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: You saw that? The touch? That's what we're up against in three weeks. Tomorrow you play.
Back inside, still catching your breath, {teacher} reads the groups off a list she clearly made before anyone could lobby.

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: {player}, {friend}, {rival}. Topic: sharing a pizza — fractions in real life. Six minutes, three speakers, Wednesday.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: Us and {rival}. In one group. For fractions.

lines.speaker: rival
lines.text: I'm doing the intro. I'm good at intros.

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: You'll decide that together. That's the point.
Cones already out, the far field still wet. {coach} stops you before you've reached the group.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: One thing this week. Just one. Before the ball arrives, look. Where's the pressure, where's your first touch going. Then receive.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Saturday you'll get that moment ten times and not notice it once unless you decide to. I'll ask you on Monday how many you noticed.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: He said the same thing to me for a month. Then it just — happened.

response.speaker: coach
response.text: Over the shoulder the ball isn't coming from. Nearest opponent, nearest teammate, then the ball. Half a second. Good question.

choices.label: Nod and get on with it

lines.text: Three cards each, a paper pizza cut into eighths, and {teacher} with a stopwatch she swears she won't look at.

lines.speaker: rival
lines.text: Intro's mine. Unless someone wants to fight about it. Nobody wants to fight about it.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: I'll do whichever bit has the least talking.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: You pick. I trust you. Just don't give me the ending, I always rush the ending.

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: Six minutes. Everyone speaks. If someone gets stuck, that's the group's problem, not theirs.
The last card goes down with time to spare. Accuracy {gp_accuracy}, clarity {gp_clarity}, teamwork {gp_teamwork} — {teacher} writes them where the group can see.

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: That's a group that listened to each other. Three voices, one presentation. Well done, all three.

lines.speaker: rival
lines.text: We should've done this at recess. Same thing. Look before it arrives.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: Did {rival} just — was that a compliment? To us?
It gets to the end. Accuracy {gp_accuracy}, clarity {gp_clarity}, teamwork {gp_teamwork}. Somewhere in the middle a card went missing and the pizza briefly had nine slices.

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: Correct in the important places. Next time, hand over instead of talking over — you'll hear the difference.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: Nine slices. I'm never living that down.
It falls apart in the middle and doesn't quite come back. Accuracy {gp_accuracy}, clarity {gp_clarity}, teamwork {gp_teamwork}. {teacher} writes them down anyway; that's the deal.

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: You'll redo the middle section for me on Friday — just the three of you, no audience. Not a punishment. A second go.

lines.speaker: rival
lines.text: That was bad. That was all of us being bad, to be fair.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: Friday. Okay. We can do Friday.
The stopwatch {teacher} wasn't going to look at beeps. Two cards still in your hand. Accuracy {gp_accuracy}, clarity {gp_clarity}, teamwork {gp_teamwork}.

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: Six minutes is part of the assignment. What you finished was good — finish it Friday, without the audience.

lines.speaker: rival
lines.text: My intro was too long. Say it. It was too long.
You stop, and don't start again, and after a long second {rival} and {friend} finish it as a pair. {teacher} watches you sit down and writes something short.

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: The two of you: good recovery. {player}: see me at lunch. Not in trouble. Just see me.

lines.speaker: rival
lines.text: Nerves. Happens. Didn't think it'd happen to you.
Dishes done. The training bag is by the door for tomorrow. The friendly is Saturday and {coach}'s one thing is still sitting in your head like a song.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: Presentation went how it went — I heard the short version. Tomorrow's training. Tonight's yours. What's it going to be?

choices.label: Twenty minutes against the wall — look, then touch

response.speaker: parent
response.text: Twenty. I'm timing it. And if the neighbours knock, that's your conversation.
Twenty minutes of the same small thing: glance, receive, glance. The wall does not care. It's oddly restful.

response.speaker: parent
response.text: Look at you. A grown-up answer. Bed by nine and I won't mention it to anyone.

lines.text: Monday, homeroom, the same orange smell. A week ago you were the new one. Now you're the one who played Saturday.

lines.speaker: rival
lines.text: Heard you played the friendly. {score}, {friend} said. I'm not saying anything about it until we play you.

lines.speaker: rival
lines.text: {friend} said you didn't play Saturday. Everything okay?
Text from {coach}, forwarded by {friend} with eleven exclamation marks: 'Ask {player} how many times they looked before it arrived. I counted {lesson_faced}. {lesson_strong} of them proper.'
Text from {coach}, via {friend}: '{lesson_faced} of those moments on Saturday. Some looked, some didn't. Tuesday we do it again.'
Text from {coach}, via {friend}: '{lesson_faced} of those moments Saturday. Ball arrived before the look, most of them. Not a telling-off. Tuesday.'
Text from {coach}, via {friend}: 'Didn't get that moment much Saturday. It'll come. Keep looking.'

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: Also — everyone still talking about you winning Knockout. {rival} hasn't lost since. It's been a long week for the rest of us.

lines.speaker: rival
lines.text: You're playing today, though. Actually playing. Not walking off halfway.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: Wednesday's still bugging me a bit. Not the grade. The bit where you just — went.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: You know what {rival} said to me after Wednesday? 'Your friend covered for me.' Just that. Then walked off like it hurt to say.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: Morning car: 'Wall on Wednesday, friendly on Saturday, Monday already. Bag's by the door. Eat something.'

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: Morning car: 'Early night Wednesday and you were actually awake for breakfast Saturday. Noted. Eat something.'

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: New project Friday. Different groups. {rival}, you're not doing the intro this time.

lines.speaker: rival
lines.text: Knockout at recess. Tight space this time — half the grass. You in, or scouting?

response.speaker: rival
response.text: Good. Half the grass, same rules. Move before it comes.
Three weeks until Batavia plays Sonoran. Two desks between you until then.

choices.label: "Tomorrow. Today I owe {friend} a rematch at the wall."

response.speaker: friend
response.text: Rematch. Yes. Bring the bad foot.

response.speaker: rival
response.text: Tomorrow, then. I'll save you a strike.
